definition: Self-report refers to a way of measuring symptoms in which people provide information about their own experiences by answering items on a questionnaire or scale. In this context, it is used to screen for and estimate the severity of depression-related symptoms based on the person’s own responses.

reasons: The packet supports the IDS-SR as a self-report instrument, but it does not support a general dictionary definition of “self-report” as a measurement method in which people answer questionnaire or scale items about their own experiences.

The added statement that it is used to screen for and estimate the severity of depression-related symptoms is specific to the IDS-SR and is not supported as the general sense of the term “self-report.”

The definition goes beyond the packet by generalizing from one instrument to the broader term, and it also shifts the sense toward depression screening rather than the cognition-related entry requested.

The definition’s first sentence makes a general claim that self-report is a method where people provide information about their own experiences; the packet does not explicitly describe self-report in that way (it only describes the IDS-SR instrument as a “self-report instrument” and “scale”).

Although the packet supports that the specific instrument (IDS-SR) is designed for “screening and assessing depression severity,” it does not support the broader wording that self-report, in general, is “used to screen for and estimate the severity of depression-related symptoms” based on people’s own responses.
